\chapter{La Bebo --- The Pronoun Tells the Truth}
\label{ch:pronoun-evidence}
\hlchaptermodality{144}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can use an object pronoun to reveal a gender the article hides.}

Complete ES-C55-la-bebo: say la bebo for el agua and explain why the pronoun can report a gender the article hides.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[la bebo]{la bebo — the pronoun tells the truth}

\label{lesson:ES-C55-la-bebo}



\begin{quote}
Which article does \emph{agua} take? (\emph{El}.) And what gender is \emph{agua} really? (\textbf{Feminine} — the article is a sound rule, not a gender.)
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: a third witness}]
When you met \emph{el agua} you were given two proofs that the word is feminine underneath: the adjective it takes and the plural it forms. Here is a third, and it costs you nothing new.

\begin{quote}
\emph{Bebo \textbf{el agua}.} — I drink the water. \emph{\textbf{La} bebo.} — I drink it.
\end{quote}

Not \emph{lo bebo}. \textbf{La} bebo.

The article had to say \emph{el} for a reason that has nothing to do with gender — two \emph{a} sounds colliding. The pronoun is under no such pressure. Nothing sits in front of it, no vowels collide, so it reports the gender straight.

This is worth more than one word. \textbf{When an article looks suspicious, the object pronoun is a witness that cannot be leaned on.} You now have a test you can run yourself, rather than a list to trust.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textquotedblleft{}el agua\textquotedblright{} then \textquotedblleft{}la bebo\textquotedblright{} — until the clash stops feeling like an error
  \item \textquotedblleft{}lo bebo\textquotedblright{} then \textquotedblleft{}la bebo\textquotedblright{}, and notice which one is about water
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
\emph{El agua} — which pronoun replaces it? (\textbf{La}.) And why does that not contradict the article? (The article changed for \textbf{sound}, not gender.)
\end{tcolorbox}
